entries.statement: Namib sand sea was a negative control for the Moon run. It scored at percentile 90.2, where the pre-registered maximum was 25.0.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: A flat sand sea is not like a polar lunar ridge, yet it ranked high. The score picks up broad terrain traits and cannot tell a poor analog from a good one.

entries.statement: Rub' al Khali was a negative control for the Moon run. It scored at percentile 75.6, where the pre-registered maximum was 25.0.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: A flat sand sea is not like a polar lunar ridge, yet it ranked high. The score picks up broad terrain traits and cannot tell a poor analog from a good one.

entries.statement: Both Mars negative controls were gated out, so the control test could not be run for Mars.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: There is no control result for Mars, so nothing shows whether the Mars ranking separates good from poor matches.

entries.statement: The Mars primary site median was percentile 61.3, below the pre-registered minimum of 90.0.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Known Mars analog sites did not rank consistently high. Mars stays a low-confidence secondary result.

entries.statement: The Moon primary site criterion could not be tested: only 1 primary site could be scored.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: The Moon ranking has no passed test on known analog sites. Lonar was gated out because its ground is vegetated or farmed.

entries.statement: For the Moon, removing the illumination weight leaves the top 1% of tiles unchanged (overlap 1.0000).
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: The Moon score is effectively terrain only. Polar lighting, a defining feature of the target, plays no part in the ranking.

entries.statement: Earth slope is not corrected for the map projection, so east-west slopes read too steep toward the equator and too gentle toward the poles.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Slope is the heaviest family in the Moon score and is biased by latitude. A latitude band check was run to see whether the ranking holds.

entries.statement: Only 0.6444 of land tiles have terrain data. Tiles without terrain are never scored.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Large parts of the Earth, mainly at high latitude, cannot appear in the search.

entries.statement: Terrain changes source at the northern edge of the main elevation dataset. Roughness steps up across that seam.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Scores near and beyond the seam partly reflect a change of data source, not a change of ground.

entries.statement: 11 of the sites v1 used have coordinates that were not confirmed from a primary source.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Site results are provisional until the coordinates are confirmed.

entries.source: NASA Moon fact sheet; NASA Mars fact sheet; NASA Glenn atmosphere model; Pandey 2020
entries.statement: Air pressure. Target: vacuum Moon (night surface pressure 3 x 10^-15 bar); Mars 6.36 mb at mean radius, under 1% of Earth. Earth: about half sea level on the highest roads (Umling La 5,798 m about 48%, NASA Glenn formula).
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Earth always has far more air than the Moon or Mars. Heat loss, dust and descent differ.

entries.source: Paige 2010; Diviner 2020 post; Hayne; WMO; Scambos 2018
entries.statement: Cold traps. Target: below 110 K (cold trapping water over a billion years); Diviner measured surface bolometric brightness temperatures as low as 29 K at mid-day in southern summer (Paige et al. 2010, Science 330:479, doi 10.1126/science.1187726, checked against a text copy, to confirm in the Science PDF). The coldest Diviner reading anywhere is 25 K in Hermite crater near the NORTH pole in winter night (not for a south pole target). South pole winter or annual minimum not sourced. Earth: 2-m air record 184.0 K (-89.2 C, Vostok, 21 Jul 1983, WMO); satellite snow-surface minimum about 174.6 K (Scambos 2018 GRL; the exact -98.6 C value, its date and the MODIS version are UNVERIFIED).
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Earth has no lunar-style cold traps, so ice-related analogies do not carry over.

entries.statement: Electrostatic dust. Target: provisional. Earth: no global Earth data.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: No Earth dataset describes charged dust, so its effects are not covered.

entries.source: NASA Moon fact sheet; NASA Mars fact sheet; Fudali 1980; Foucher 2021
entries.statement: Gravity. Target: 1.62 m/s2 Moon; Mars mean surface gravity 3.73 m/s2 (3.71 m/s2 is the equatorial value). Earth: 9.81 everywhere.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Gravity cannot be matched anywhere on Earth. Mobility, dust and structure behave differently on the Moon and Mars.

entries.statement: Line of sight to Earth, GPS. Target: Earth line of sight is an Artemis III site criterion; Earth GPS and Galileo signals are weak but were tracked on the lunar surface once (NASA LuGRE, 3 March 2025). Earth: always available.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Earth always has a view of Earth and satellites; the Moon does not.

entries.statement: Oxidants. Target: 0.5-1 wt% perchlorate on Mars. Earth: up to 0.6 wt% in the Atacama.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Mars soil oxidants are only partly matched on Earth.

entries.source: NASA SVS 4893; PGDA product 69; Mazarico; Glaser
entries.statement: Polar lighting. Target: Sun within about 1.5 deg of the horizon all year, 18.6-year cycle. Earth: low Sun in polar spring and autumn only (pole Sun reaches 23.4 deg).
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Earth has only partial matches to lunar polar lighting, and the score does not use it.

entries.source: WHO UV; Kiel via ScienceDaily; Pandey; Harris
entries.statement: Radiation and UV. Target: no shielding; lunar surface particle dose about 60 microsieverts per hour. Earth: UV rises about 10 percent per 1000 m of altitude (WHO); ground particle dose more than 200 times lower than on the Moon, not zero.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Earth's surface radiation is far lower, so exposure cannot be rehearsed realistically.

entries.statement: Regolith. Target: unweathered, glass-welded, dry except in cold traps. Earth: weathered, oxidised, damp ash and basalt.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Earth soils are weathered and damp; lunar regolith is not.

entries.statement: Regolith mechanics (grain size, density, abrasiveness). Target: provisional. Earth: no global Earth data.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Grain size, density and abrasiveness are not covered by any Earth dataset used.

entries.statement: Rock chemistry. Target: iron-rich Martian basalt; lunar anorthosite. Earth: basalt 45-52% silica; anorthosite rare.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Earth rarely matches lunar or Martian rock chemistry.

entries.statement: Sterility. Target: no known life. Earth: 1.7-13.6 million cells per gram in desert cores.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: Earth deserts carry microbial life; Mars is treated as sterile for planning.

entries.statement: dust index is not scored for Mars. Mars dust cover and the Earth atmospheric dust column are different things.
entries.what_this_means_for_the_analogy: A property that matters for the analogy is missing from the score, so the score cannot show whether it matches.

meta.label: Where v1 failed and where Earth differs from the Moon and Mars. Most entries are provisional.
limits: Entries describe limits and failures. None of them describes a success.
Most physical differences come from a draft v1 ledger whose entries are provisional and not verified by us.
Source wording is quoted as stored. Some entries were checked by chat assistants and not re-verified.
The list is not complete. It covers what v1 recorded.
meta.uncertainty_sentence: The Monte Carlo varies the weights and, for the Moon only, the slope and relief measurement error, and applies no systematic Earth bias to any of the 15 Earth columns, so the reported score bands and robust-tile counts understate the real uncertainty.
